assertion_analysis.fails_if: len(builds) is not 1; a fresh readiness cache per launch makes project_section_readiness run three times (observed as [1,1,1] in negative-control.log), so this reddens on the exact regression it was added for.
len(builds) is not 2; if the key ignored a plan's mtime the touched plan would still hit the cache and the count would stay 1, so this guards the fingerprint's mtime component.

the direct dispatch reused the pass cache (a module-global cache would drop the count to 1); the literal 3 also encodes an internal two-cache count and reddens if the direct path legitimately changes how many caches it builds.

the pass's cached launch results differ from an uncached dispatch_waits computation for the same nodes; a shared cache that returned stale or wrong rows would make the two sides diverge — but both sides call the same function, so it does not guard dispatch_waits correctness itself.

findings.text: _plan_tree_fingerprint reimplements the plan-state cache identity the repository already owns at reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py:236 roadmap_project_generation (HEAD + covered-directory shape via _covered_directory_shape, :171), which also covers every PLAN_HTML_PREFIXES directory; extend that owner rather than globbing only docs/plans/*.html, so an edit to a plan document outside docs/plans also invalidates a pass's cached rows.

_readiness_rows recomputes the fingerprint before every cache lookup, so each launch spawns git rev-parse HEAD and stats every docs/plans/*.html (212 files in this checkout) about twice (once in _validated_batch_waits, once in dispatch_waits) even on a hit; compute it once per project per pass, or use the owner's per-directory covered_dir_identity, to keep the stat volume off GPFS.
